sentences.text: Zuul is an extinct herbivorous ankylosaurine dinosaur belonging to the family Ankylosauridae and the subfamily Ankylosaurinae.
It is the first ankylosaurine known from both a complete skull and a complete tail club, with a skull measuring approximately 50 centimeters long.
The skull features a wide, flat snout that is cut off at the front, and the armor tiles on the head overlap and point upward.
This animal was estimated to reach a total length of six meters and weigh 2.5 tons.
The tail itself measures a total length of 278 centimeters.
Zuul holds the record for the longest tail club shaft among North American ankylosaurids, measuring 210 centimeters including the handle.
Fossil remains of keratinous scales like those found on Zuul are extremely rare.
The holotype was discovered in 2014 near Havre, Montana, while a company excavated a potential Gorgosaurus specimen.
The skeleton was found when a truck carrying a twelve-meter-high load accidentally struck a tail club of an ankylosaur.
Arbour and Evans described Zuul in 2017 based on a phylogenetic analysis and named the genus Zuul and the species Zuul crurivastator.
The skeleton was found lying on its back in a rotated position.
By 2017, only the tail of the Zuul skeleton had been prepared for study.
The species name crurivastator means "Destroyer of Shins," referring to the animal's presumed tactic of smashing predators' legs with its tail club.
Researchers suggest that Zuul used its tail club to smash the lower legs of attacking predators as a defensive tactic.
The phylogenetic analysis of Zuul yielded inconclusive results regarding the exact interrelationships of ankylosaurins, largely influenced by the placement of Anodontosaurus and Ziapelta.
Phylogenetic trees recovered for Zuul show nine out of ten place it as the sister group of Dyoplosaurus, while one tree places it closer to Anodontosaurus.
Zuul lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 75 million years ago, in what is now North America.
The specimen was found in the Judith River Formation, specifically the middle Coal Ridge Member, dating between 76.2 and 75.2 million years ago.
